title: Through the Wicker Latch
story:
The blue pickup truck's engine sputtered to life, sending a low vibration through the dusty gravel shoulder, but the vehicle remained stationary as the driver paused to check a paper logbook on his dashboard. James didn't hesitate. Slipping down from the split-rail wooden fence, he sprinted low across the ground, staying hidden in the shadow cast by the heavy rear bumper.

Scrambling silently up the spare tire mounted underneath, James pulled himself over the tailgate into the truck bed. The heavy wooden crate resting atop Nico's basket made lifting the cover impossible from above. Reaching into his satchel, James retrieved his weathered leather strap bound with colorful woven threads and looped the sturdy band tightly around the tapered wooden peg securing the basket latch.

Bracing his feet against the pine sideboards, James pulled with all his strength. With a firm, desperate tug, James unlatched the wooden basket lid on the stationary truck bed using his leather strap, freeing Nico before they both escaped into the surrounding brush. The little deer mouse scrambled out of the dark basket with a quiet squeak and leaped onto James's shoulder just as the peg popped loose.

Before the driver could gear into motion, James grabbed his strap and vaulted over the tailgate. They hit the soft earth running and ducked into a dense hedge of honeysuckle, watching from the cool leafy shade as the truck finally roared away down the highway, leaving a lingering trail of dust in the bright morning air. Safe once more, James sat in the quiet shade, letting his breathing settle as Nico snuggled close against his side.
location: A thick honeysuckle hedge near a roadside produce stand south of San Antonio del Río
